content.value_statement: Genkit projects can fail when APIs, model names, and provider setup drift. This skill guides Node.js and TypeScript developers with current setup, examples, and troubleshooting steps.
actual_capabilities: Guides Genkit CLI version checks and documentation lookup commands.
Shows Genkit initialization with Google AI provider and Gemini models.
Provides examples for text generation, structured output, streaming, image generation, and speech generation.
Explains migration issues from pre-1.0 Genkit APIs.
Describes a setup workflow for ai directories, package scripts, and provider environment variables.
limitations: Requires the Genkit CLI, project dependencies, and provider credentials to be available.
Defaults to Google AI when the user does not choose a provider.
Other providers require documentation lookup before installation and configuration.
General setup steps may need changes for unusual project layouts.

best_practices: Verify Genkit CLI documentation before changing code that depends on current APIs.
Keep provider keys in environment variables and never hardcode them.
Run type checks after changes and map failures to known Genkit error patterns.
anti_patterns: Using pre-1.0 Genkit imports or global configuration patterns.
Hardcoding provider credentials, model assumptions, or unsupported media formats.
Creating broad tools or flows that mix unrelated responsibilities.

faq.question: Which projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Node.js and TypeScript projects that use Genkit for AI flows, tools, and generation features.

faq.question: Does it only work with Google AI?
faq.answer: No. It defaults to Google AI, but it directs users to provider documentation for OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and others.

faq.question: Can it fix Genkit migration errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers common v1.x migration issues for imports, models, response access, streaming, and flow definitions.

faq.question: Does it store API keys?
faq.answer: No. It recommends environment variables and reminds users to configure provider keys outside source code.

faq.question: Will it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides command guidance for setup, docs, and type checks. Execution depends on the active coding agent and user approval model.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide your project type, provider choice, relevant errors, and the Genkit feature you want to build or debug.
